title: klayout-tools netlist-driven layout plan request
description: klt.layout_plan.request/1 (issue #1131, Phase B of docs/design/netlist-driven-layout-spike.md section 2). A plan does not describe geometry -- it describes intent: which netlist devices form a matched group, what topology that group uses, what order groups occupy in a row, and which groups must abut. See docs/cli/layout-plan.md and src/klayout_tools/layout_plan.py (validate_layout_plan) for the reference validator this schema documents. Executing a plan (generation) is a separate, not-yet-built follow-up (spike section 4, Phase C).

schema.description: Contract identifier + major version. Not enforced by the reference validator (see layout_plan.py) -- present here for documentation/tooling that wants to check it.

netlist.description: The same path/top/form/deck/device_map shape klt lvs's reference-side request already accepts (docs/cli/lvs.md) -- a plan resolves its netlist through the identical ingestion path. An unrecognised key is a usage error, mirroring pdk's own unknown-key check.

path.description: Path to the netlist SPICE file, parsed via klt lvs's own reference-netlist reader.

top.description: The circuit to digest. Omit when the netlist has exactly one top-level circuit.

form.description: "plain-element" (default) reads the file as-is. "subckt-call" converts a real PDK schematic flow's simulation-form netlist first (klayout_tools.netlist_normalize).

deck.description: Only used with form: "subckt-call". "sky130"/"gf180mcu" -- selects that deck's curated device-name map for the conversion.

device_map.description: Only used with form: "subckt-call". Explicit <subckt-name> -> <device_class> overrides, merged on top of deck's curated table -- the same shape klt lvs's reference.device_map accepts (docs/cli/lvs.md). Every entry is currently resolved as a MOS-shaped (4-terminal) override; a non-MOS subcircuit name raises a clear error instead of a silent misbind.

pdk.description: The exact fields klt gen/klt gen-compose already accept -- one resolver, no exception for plans. Validated for shape only at Phase B; resolution against an installed PDK is deferred to plan execution (Phase C).

device_groups.description: One entry per matched/placed unit. May be empty (no groups declared yet).

id.description: Caller-chosen label, addressed elsewhere in rows/abutment/encloses -- mirrors klt gen-compose's blocks[].id. Unique within device_groups.

oneOf.description: A bare netlist device instance name (the ingestion digest's devices[].name). Valid only when that name is unambiguous across device classes in the digest; a name carried by two or more classes must use the qualified object form instead.
A class-qualified device reference -- the same name + class pairing klt lvs's mismatches[].device already uses.

name.description: The digest's devices[].name for this device.

device_class.description: The digest's devices[].device_class for this device (e.g. "PFET", "RES"). Omit to resolve by name alone, which requires that name to be unambiguous.

devices.description: Netlist device instances (from the ingestion digest, klayout_tools.netlist_digest) this group is generated from. A digest device name is per-class, not circuit-global -- NetlistSpiceReader strips the leading SPICE element-type letter ("M1" -> "1", "R1" -> "1"), so "1" can name a MOS device and a resistor in the same circuit. Each entry is therefore either a bare name string or a {name, device_class} object; an unresolvable reference, a device_class that does not exist for that name, and a bare name that is ambiguous across classes are all application errors, exit code 1. Empty for a group like a guard ring that encloses other groups rather than wrapping specific devices.

generator.description: Which existing klt gen generator produces this group's geometry (docs/cli/gen.md's existing set -- resistor_strip, mos_array, res_array, cap_array, guard_ring, diff_pair, bjt_array, bond_pad, esd_device). A plan invents no new generator; naming one klt gen does not have is an application error, exit code 1.

topology.description: The matching pattern for this group. "array"/"common_centroid" map onto the topology param mos_array/bjt_array already accept; diff_pair always lays out "common_centroid". "interdigitated"/"single" are proposed values no generator supports yet -- declaring either (on any generator) is flagged as an application error, exit code 1, not silently accepted. See docs/cli/layout-plan.md.

dummy.description: Leading/trailing or row/col dummy-element counts -- routed to the named generator's own dummy_rows/dummy_cols-style param at execution time (Phase C). Not deeply validated at Phase B.

encloses.description: For an enclosure-shaped generator (guard_ring): which other device_groups[].id values it must surround. Each id must resolve to a declared device_groups[].id (other than its own); an unresolvable id is an application error, exit code 1.

params.description: Generator-specific overrides layered on top of parameters plan execution (Phase C) resolves automatically from the ingested netlist's own device sizing. Not deeply validated at Phase B.

order.description: device_groups[].id values placed left-to-right in this row. Each id must resolve to a declared device_groups[].id -- an unresolvable id is an application error, exit code 1.

spacing_um.description: Horizontal gap between adjacent groups in this row -- same semantics as klt gen-compose's placement.spacing_um.

align.description: Vertical alignment of this row's groups relative to each other.

abutment.description: Pairs of groups that must share an edge with a caller-declared gap_um rather than being connected by a routed net.

a.description: A device_groups[].id. Must resolve to a declared id, and must differ from b -- an unresolvable id or a==b is an application error, exit code 1.

b.description: A device_groups[].id. Must resolve to a declared id, and must differ from a -- an unresolvable id or a==b is an application error, exit code 1.

edge.description: Which edge of a touches b.

gap_um.description: Gap between the two groups' declared edge, typically 0.0 for a true abutment.

options.description: Same semantics as klt gen-compose's own options fields.
